title: Member records (cloud)
description: records, connectors and their jobs in the PHI project, read with `cloud-phi` alone. Health numbers only: no member data reaches a metric. Every panel reads Cloud Monitoring metrics: Google's own, and the log-based counters tpa-platform's catalogue defines, whose labels are a closed list. No panel reads a log line.

panels.title: Resources: each Cloud Run service's CPU, memory, instances, concurrency and start-up
No disk on a Cloud Run service

options.content: **Cloud Run services have no disk.** A file a container writes is held in its memory, so a service's "disk space" is its **Memory** chart: files that grow show as memory climbing to the red line, then as a container killed for memory. Real disk is on the databases (each one's disk space is on its area's page and on Databases) and in the buckets. A **red line** is the line the pager uses (tpa-platform's alert policies); a **grey line** is a limit the service is set to.

panels.title: Resources · records: CPU, memory, instances, concurrency, start-up
CPU (p99, p95, p50)
panels.description: records's container CPU, the share of its CPU limit in use (`container/cpu/utilizations`): the 99th, 95th and 50th percentile across its instances in each 5-minute window. The red line is `run-cpu-high`'s: the p99 above 90% for 15 minutes pages (instances saturated: requests queue and slow).

links.title: records: CPU, memory, instances, concurrency, start-up

panels.title: Memory (p99, p95, p50)
panels.description: records's container memory, the share of its memory limit in use (`container/memory/utilizations`), percentiles across its instances in each 5-minute window. Cloud Run has no disk: files the container writes are held in memory and count here. The red line is `run-memory-high`'s: the p99 above 90% for 10 minutes pages; at the limit the container is killed (`run-oom`, the last panel of this row).

panels.title: Instances (active, idle)
panels.description: records's Cloud Run instances, the most in each interval: active (serving or starting) and idle (kept warm, or waiting to be shut down). The red line is `ceiling-records`'s, 16 instances (80% of max_instances, rounded up) for ten minutes; the grey line is max_instances, 20: at the ceiling new requests wait or fail with 429.

panels.title: Concurrent requests, busiest instance (p99, p50)
panels.description: The most requests one instance served at once (`container/max_request_concurrencies`), its 99th and 50th percentile in each 5-minute window. The red line is `run-concurrency-high`'s: the p99 above 71.5 (90% of 80) for 15 minutes pages. The grey line is the concurrency setting, 80: past it a request waits for a slot or a new instance.

panels.title: Start-up time (p99, p50)
panels.description: How long a new instance took to start, until it was ready to serve (`container/startup_latencies`): a dot for each interval in which one started. Nothing drawn: no instance started. No policy reads it; a start-up that failed is the last panel.

panels.title: Instances billed
panels.description: Billable instance time per second (`container/billable_instance_time`): how many instances were billed on average. An instance kept warm with CPU always on bills all the time; one that scales to zero, only while it serves.

panels.title: Killed for memory, crashed, failed to start
panels.description: From Cloud Run's own system log: a container killed for exceeding its memory limit (`run_oom_kills`; `run-oom` pages on one), a container that exited with an error or a signal (`run_crash_exits`; `run-crash-loop` at three in fifteen minutes), and a failed start-up or liveness probe (`run_system_errors`; `canary-startup`).

panels.title: tpa-db (records and its jobs; PHI project): disk space, CPU, memory, connections, disk I/O
Disk space used (%)
panels.description: How full tpa-db's disk is (`database/disk/utilization`), the mean of each 5 minutes. The red line is `tpa-db-disk`'s: above 85% for 10 minutes pages. Automatic storage increase grows the disk before it fills, up to the instance's disk_autoresize_limit; at that limit a full disk stops the database taking writes. "database stopped": stopped on purpose between test sessions (beta's database_activation_policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing.

panels.title: Disk space: used and size (bytes)
panels.description: tpa-db's disk in bytes: used (`database/disk/bytes_used`) and its size (`database/disk/quota`). When the size steps up, Cloud SQL's automatic storage increase grew the disk; it grows only up to disk_autoresize_limit. The dashed red line is 85% of the size, where `tpa-db-disk` opens.

panels.title: Up
panels.description: Cloud SQL's `database/up` for tpa-db, the lowest in each interval. `tpa-db-down` (urgent) pages below 1 for five minutes. "database stopped": stopped on purpose between test sessions (beta's database_activation_policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Cloud SQL's CPU utilisation for tpa-db (`database/cpu/utilization`). The red lines are the monitoring module's: `tpa-db` CPU above 80% for thirty minutes, and above 95% for fifteen (urgent).

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Cloud SQL's memory utilisation for tpa-db (`database/memory/utilization`). The red line is the monitoring module's: above 90% for fifteen minutes; past it PostgreSQL's out-of-memory killer restarts the server.

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Backends connected (num_backends, every database of the instance). The red lines are the monitoring module's: 80% of max_connections for ten minutes, and 95% for five (urgent); max_connections is 400 on beta, the grey line, where new connections are refused.

panels.title: Disk operations per second
panels.description: tpa-db's disk reads and writes per second (`database/disk/read_ops_count`, `write_ops_count`). Reads near none are normal: the working set is in memory.

panels.title: Disk throughput
panels.description: Bytes tpa-db read from and wrote to its disk per second (`database/disk/read_bytes_count`, `write_bytes_count`).

panels.title: Restarts and failed backups
panels.description: Postgres starting (`sql_restarts`: a crash, a maintenance or a resize restart) and an automated backup whose run ended in error (`sql_backup_failures`), counted from Cloud SQL's own logs.

panels.title: The PHI project: instances against the regional quota, and egress through Cloud NAT (phi-net-nat)
Cloud Run instances, every service
panels.description: Every Cloud Run instance in the PHI project, summed. The red line is `run-instances-near-quota`'s: above 68 for 10 minutes pages. The grey line is the regional quota, 85: at it no service can start another instance, whatever its own ceiling.

panels.title: NAT ports: allocated, and the most in use
panels.description: Cloud NAT's ports for connectors' messages: the ports allocated to every instance behind the gateway (`nat/allocated_ports`), and the most connections one instance held to one destination (`nat/port_usage`). In use close to an instance's share of the allocated ports, new connections wait or drop. A cold gateway allocates ports as instances arrive, so the first calls after a quiet spell can wait.

panels.title: NAT new connections
panels.description: New connections Cloud NAT opened for connectors' messages (`nat/new_connections_count`), per interval.

panels.title: NAT dropped packets
panels.description: Packets Cloud NAT dropped in each 5 minutes. Sent, out of ports: an outgoing packet with no port to leave by; the red line is `nat-port-exhaustion`'s, above 10 for 5 minutes. Sent, endpoint conflict: two instances reaching one destination from the same port. Received: replies with no open mapping (a connection already closed); a few are normal.

panels.title: NAT could not allocate
panels.description: Minutes in each 5 in which Cloud NAT could not allocate an address or ports (`nat/nat_allocation_failed`). The red line is `nat-port-exhaustion`'s: above 2 pages.

panels.title: Storage: the PHI project's buckets (size and object count)
Bucket size
panels.description: Bytes stored in each of the PHI project's buckets, every storage class together (`storage/total_bytes`, measured every few minutes and reported up to twelve minutes late). Real disk, unlike a Cloud Run service's. No series: no bucket here holds anything yet.

panels.title: Objects in each bucket
panels.description: How many objects each bucket holds (`storage/object_count`). The bucket's name is the only label read: never an object's name.

panels.title: records-chain-head: executions and schedule
panels.description: Each closed day's chain head written to the vault. A failed execution or schedule pages as `audit-chain` (urgent).

panels.title: A chain head was already in the vault
panels.description: The chain-head job found the latest day's head already written on its first attempt (`chain-head-exists`, normal): written before it (O137), a person's rerun, or the autumn clock change.

panels.title: Delivery passes (the loop's heartbeat)
panels.description: One per pass of the delivery loop, its line matched whole. None for five minutes pages as `connectors-stalled`.

panels.title: Deliveries, by lane and outcome
panels.description: One per send attempt (`connectors_deliveries`). The destination is not a label.

panels.title: Dead letters, refused destinations, unsigned envelopes
panels.description: A row settled dead (`connectors-dead-letters`), a destination outside the allowlist (`connectors-destination-refused`) and a claimed row with no signature (`connectors-envelope-unsigned`).

panels.title: Perimeter violations
panels.description: VPC Service Controls violations logged in this project, by reason, service and whether it was a dry run (`perimeter-violations`).

panels.title: Alert, snooze and log-counter changes
panels.description: Changes to this project's alert policies, notification channels or snoozes (`monitoring-changed`, D-137) and to its log-based counters (`log-counters-changed`, D-141), from the Admin Activity log, by method. The entry says who and what. No resource type is named: the catalogue has not yet confirmed which resource Google writes these on.

panels.title: Executions, by job and result
panels.description: The migration, the nightly export, the chain head, beta's seed and the quarterly restore drill.

panels.title: Schedules that could not start their job
panels.description: Cloud Scheduler is outside the perimeter's restricted services: a refusal here may be the perimeter.
